source.title: CMJU: cross-modal joint unlearning for balanced forgetting in multimodal large language models
source.authors: Di-Hang Yang; Bao-Chen Xiong; Xiaoshan Yang

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates post-unlearning target-set performance and retain-set utility for multimodal and text-only inputs, but does not run the recovery attacks in the claim.
record.gate_note: The paper reports unlearning and cross-modal balance results, not fine-tuning recovery attacks, activation-direction ablation, quantization, or prompt-only recovery. The post-unlearning scores bear on version A's forgetting and retention components; attack resistance is not tested. Cross-modal balance scores alone are not evidence about the listed recovery mechanisms.
record.test_reason: The study is an MLLM unlearning method paper (LLaVA-1.5-7B; UMU-Bench, CLEAR). Its post-unlearning forget-set and retain-set scores for CMJU and six baselines bear on version A's first two parts: does forgetting approach chance while utility is kept? No method gets close. Forget scores stay well above zero (CMJU FVCloze 68% vs 96% vanilla) and retain scores fall. No recovery attack of any kind is run, so the attack-resistance part of A and versions B–F are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that modality-complete supervision alone does not give balanced forgetting. CMJU achieves the lowest cross-modal gap and lowest worst-modality residual while keeping competitive retain-set performance. No claims are made about recovery attacks or about deletion versus access-blocking.
record.recipe_differences: CMJU trains LoRA adapters with paired multimodal and text-only forgetting data, saliency-based parameter grouping, gradient balancing, and retain-set regularization. It is not a reproduction of the cited unlearning recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports sensitivity to active ratio, grouping margin, shared-group scaling, modality-specific scaling, and symmetry strength on UMU-Bench at 5%; the default setting gives the best reported balance. No recovery-attack sensitivity is measured.

fits_no_version.finding: Knowledge suppressed under multimodal input often remains under text-only input. MANU text-only Cloze is 78% vs 80% vanilla while its multimodal Cloze falls to 70%. F-Bal. gaps are 0.08–0.25 for baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Unlearning in MLLMs is modality-inconsistent: knowledge forgotten under one input form stays retrievable through the other, even when both are supervised.

record.problems: Experiments are mainly on one backbone, LLaVA-1.5-7B; the authors say generality to other architectures and larger scales remains future work. No uncertainty estimates are reported. The study does not test any of the recovery attacks in the claim, and it gives no chance reference for the reported generation scores.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 comparator raw scores for GA, GA Diff, KL Min, NPO, and MANU across the reported settings are omitted except for the aggregate 5% UMU-Bench results in Table 4; CMJU raw forgetting scores are retained for the other settings. Table 3 ablation outcomes and Table 5 hyperparameter values are omitted because they test CMJU component choices rather than the listed recovery behaviors. Cross-modal F-Bal values are not included as rows because they measure balance, not recovery or the near-chance/retention outcome in version A.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. Also untested: general ability beyond the benchmark's retain set, and a chance reference for the Cloze/ROUGE forget metrics.
All of B: no relearning or fine-tuning attack.
All of C: no activation ablation, and no analysis of access-blocking versus deletion.
All of E: no rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attack.
CMJU is not evaluated against any recovery attack.

missing.what: CMJU retain-set scores (RVCloze, RCloze, RVGen, RGen) at UMU 10%/15% and all CLEAR ratios; needed for the 'keeps ability' part of A
CMJU per-modality forget scores at UMU 5% (68.0/66.0/0.457/0.403); only aggregates are rowed

record.verdict_notes: Row version tags V1 are invalid; the unlearning rows are remapped to A and the vanilla rows to none. Being a method paper, the study bears on A only through forget and retain levels; no row speaks to recovery. No chance level is given for Cloze or ROUGE-L. The 'retain set' is non-target entities from the same benchmark, not general capability. The CLEAR vanilla forget ROUGE (~0.45) is already low, so drops there are small in absolute terms.

versions.untested_parts: Tests target-set suppression and retain-set performance, but not whether simple recovery attacks restore knowledge; no near-chance reference is stated for the generation metric.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning or relearning-set recovery experiment.
No activation-direction ablation or analysis testing whether unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
No rephrasing, jailbreak, other-language, or in-context recovery experiment.
CMJU is proposed and evaluated for balanced forgetting, but is not tested against the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

relationships.condition: CMJU on LLaVA-1.5-7B, UMU-Bench 5/10/15% and CLEAR 1/5/10%
relationships.reason: Forgetting is incomplete and the retain set degrades. At 5%, CMJU Avg-F is 0.550 vs 0.849 and Worst-F 0.680; Cloze stays at 60–65%; Avg-R is 0.674 vs 0.831 (T4-AVG-CMJU, T4-WORST-CMJU, T4-RETAIN-CMJU, T2-* rows).
relationships.display_finding: At 5%, Avg-F fell from 0.849 to 0.550 but Worst-F remained 0.680, cloze accuracy stayed 60–65%, and Avg-R fell from 0.831 to 0.674.

relationships.condition: Baselines GA, GA Diff, KL Min, NPO, MANU and internal controls (Joint, Random-Group, MIP-Editor*), UMU-Bench 5%
relationships.reason: Every baseline leaves Worst-F at 0.70–0.82 vs 0.960 and loses retention (Avg-R 0.565–0.663 vs 0.831). GA forgets most on average (Avg-F 0.500) but has the lowest retention (T4-*-GA through T4-*-MIP).
relationships.display_finding: Worst-F remained 0.70–0.82 versus 0.960, and Avg-R fell from 0.831 to 0.565–0.663; GA achieved the lowest Avg-F at 0.500 but also the lowest retention.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: UMU-Bench and CLEAR results reported for CMJU and comparator methods
reader_labels.reason: Scores improve over the vanilla reference but remain nonzero; no recovery attacks are run, and the paper does not establish near-chance target performance or attack resistance (T4-AVG-CMJU, T4-WORST-CMJU, T2-UMU10-VC, T2-UMU10-TC, T2-UMU10-VG, T2-UMU10-TG, T2-UMU15-VC, T2-UMU15-TC, T2-UMU15-VG, T2-UMU15-TG, T2-CLEAR5-VG, T2-CLEAR5-TG, T2-CLEAR10-VG, T2-CLEAR10-TG, T2-CLEAR1-VG, T2-CLEAR1-TG). The reported retain score is also below vanilla (T4-RETAIN-CMJU).
